name: Plan-and-Solve Prompting
executive_summary: Explicitly separate 'devise a plan' from 'carry out the plan' as two distinct prompted steps, rather than letting planning and execution blur together in one CoT pass.
description: Stage one produces an explicit multi-step plan for solving the problem without yet solving any step. Stage two executes the plan step by step, referencing the plan text throughout. Zero-shot, requiring no exemplars, and specifically targets CoT failure modes caused by missing steps or calculation errors from conflating planning and execution.
when_to_use: Multi-step problems where plain zero-shot CoT tends to skip steps or lose track of the overall structure.
when_not_to_use: Very short, single-step tasks where an explicit plan step is pure overhead.
known_pitfalls: An incomplete or wrong plan still constrains the execution step, similar to Least-to-Most's decomposition-quality bottleneck.

primary_source.authors: Wang, Wei, Schuurmans, Le, Chi, Narang, Chowdhery, Zhou
primary_source.title: Plan-and-Solve Prompting: Improving Zero-Shot Chain-of-Thought Reasoning by Large Language Models

{{question}}
Let's first understand the problem, extract relevant variables and their corresponding numerals, and devise a complete plan. Then, let's carry out the plan, calculate intermediate results, and solve the problem step by step.
usage_templates.reproducibility_note: A single LLM call (or a fixed sequence of them) with no external system dependency; running this template again at temperature 0 against the same model version should reproduce the same output.
